use_when: Labelling a thing that already exists — a status, a category, a credential someone holds. Sm is the status tag; Md reads as a credential.
dont_use_when: Anything clickable — and note that nothing stops you. `ChipProps` extends the span's HTML attributes and spreads them, so `onClick`, `tabIndex` and `role` all compile and all attach; on the deployed Chip the handler fires. What does not come with them is any focus appearance: `Chip.css` carries no focus rule for any tone, so a keyboard user gets a control the design never drew. Use Button for an action, and a real `<button>` or `<input type="checkbox">` for a filter the user can toggle. A section label above a heading: use Eyebrow. A sentence: the pill does not wrap the way a paragraph does — keep the chip to a word or two and put the sentence in a paragraph beside it.
placement: Inside cards, table cells, list rows, and beside headings — always attached to the thing it describes.
a11y: Non-interactive by default rather than by construction, and the difference is the whole of what this field can promise. As shipped it is a `<span>` with no role, no tabindex and no handler, so there is no focus state to make visible and none is drawn. But `ChipProps` extends `HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>` and spreads every one of those attributes onto the span, so a caller can add `role`, `tabIndex` and `onClick` — verified on the deployed build — and the component supplies no focus ring, no Enter or Space handling and no pressed state to go with them. So what it does not guarantee is that it stays non-interactive; it guarantees only that it will not help if you make it interactive. The mark is an IconSlot with no name, so it is `aria-hidden` and the text is what gets read. The label is real text, so it scales with the page and is selectable. Colour is never the only carrier of meaning — every tone ships a word beside it. Six of the eight variants fall below 4.5:1 in day mode; that is measured, ruled on, and recorded in decisions.md, not an oversight.
